post.caption: Liberty's copper skin is hammered like jewelry. The Statue of Liberty's skin is hand hammered copper. The method is called repoussé, hammering the metal from behind. Jewelers do the same with a hammer and punch on sheet gold. Sculptor Bartholdi designed it, and work began in France in 1875. Workers hammered the sheets over wooden forms. The copper is only 2.4 millimeters thick, about two pennies. More than 300 separate sheets make up the skin. Gustave Eiffel designed the iron framework that holds it up. It was dedicated in New York on October 28, 1886.
